transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, so I'm here because work has just been... well, I'm a registered nurse, and on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. It's gotten really bad. 

Like, we just got these new smart IV pumps on our unit last month, which are supposed to be so much better, but honestly, they beep just as much as the old ones. And my manager, Susan, she was saying we need to be faster with the new touchscreen interface, which is ridiculous because we're already short-staffed and the training was basically just a ten-minute video they made us watch in the breakroom... but anyway, what was I saying? 

Oh, right. So, an IV pump beeps, or I hear someone asking another nurse a question down the hall, or a call light goes off... and those call lights, I swear I hear them in my sleep now. My husband says I actually flinch when our microwave beeps at home because it sounds exactly like the bed alarms in room four. 

But yeah, one of those things happens, and suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was even working on. It just entirely vanishes from my head.
Did you have this same kind of distractibility when you were a child?

Yeah, definitely. Even way back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was constantly losing my worksheets or just completely forgetting to turn in my homework. 

I remember my fourth-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, she used to print all our math worksheets on this bright purple paper. She read somewhere that it was supposed to stimulate learning or something, but honestly, it just smelled really strongly of the copy machine. Do they even use those anymore? Probably not, with all the iPads kids have now. My niece has an iPad for first grade and she just plays Roblox on it half the time, which my sister hates, but it keeps her quiet in restaurants... 

But anyway, because I was always losing those purple papers, my mom actually had to sit with me at the kitchen table every single night. If she wasn't right there to keep me on track, nothing would get done. We had this awful floral wallpaper in that kitchen, and I would just sit there counting the little yellow daisies on it instead of doing my spelling words. I think she finally painted over it when I was in high school, thank goodness. It was such a terrible color scheme. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, being a kid. But yeah, my mom had to sit with me every night, so I guess it's always been an issue.
Outside of work, does this distractibility create major problems in your day-to-day life?

Well, outside of work... I mean, yeah, it definitely affects things at home, but honestly, work is where it's really blowing up right now. It's gotten so bad that they actually put me on formal supervision. 

Which is just... it's humiliating. I've been a nurse for almost eight years. I used to work on a med-surg floor at County General before I came here, and that place was a madhouse. We had this one doctor, Dr. Aris, who would literally throw charts if things weren't done exactly how he wanted. I mean, actual physical charts, back when we used paper. He threw one at a wall once and the metal spine dented the drywall. They had to put a poster over it because maintenance took three months to fix it. It was a poster about handwashing, I think. Or maybe fall risks? 

Anyway, sorry. The point is, I'm supposed to be a charge nurse now, but because I keep losing track of things, the other nurses have to double-check parts of my follow-through. It makes me feel like I’m becoming a liability to the unit instead of a leader. Susan, my manager, she tried to frame it as "supportive rounding," but we all know what it means. It just feels terrible knowing they can't trust me to finish what I start.
At home, do you also often lose track of what you’re doing?

Yeah, I do. It's... it's really frustrating, honestly. I forget things that should just be totally routine. Like, I'll mean to pay a bill, or I'll need to call my sister back—she's the one with the niece who plays Roblox all the time. Actually, my sister just called me yesterday because she's trying to plan a birthday party for her, and she wants to do it at this trampoline park. Have you ever been to one of those? They are a nightmare for infection control, just kids sweating all over these foam pits. I took my nephew to one years ago and he ended up with hand, foot, and mouth disease. The blisters were awful, and he couldn't eat anything but popsicles for a week. We bought out the entire grocery store's supply of those Outshine fruit bars. The strawberry ones are really good, actually, they have real chunks of fruit in them. 

But um, what was I saying? Oh, right, forgetting things. Yeah, I'll completely forget to call her back, or I'll miss an appointment, or even at work I'll forget to follow up on a missing order. And the worst part is, I meant to do it. I'll even set a reminder on my phone, and it'll go off, and I'll swipe it away thinking, "I'll do that in two seconds," and then... poof. It's gone.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

No, not really. I mean, I don't sit around worrying about random things for no reason. I get stressed out when I know I've messed up or forgotten something important, like with work right now, but I don't just worry out of nowhere. 

My mom, though, she is a huge worrier. She watches the local news every single night and gets completely worked up about everything. The other day she called me in a panic because she saw a segment on those murder hornets. Do you remember when those were all over the news a couple of years ago? The giant ones from Asia? She was convinced they were going to start building nests in her backyard because she has these big oak trees. I tried to tell her they haven't even been spotted in our state, but she wouldn't listen. She actually called a pest control guy to come spray her trees, which cost her like two hundred dollars, and it probably didn't even do anything except kill the regular bees. And we need the regular bees! I read this article about how bee populations are collapsing and if they die out, we won't have avocados anymore. I love avocados. I make this really good guacamole with red onions and a ton of cilantro... some people hate cilantro, though. They say it tastes like soap. I guess it's a genetic thing? 

But anyway, no, I don't really worry about things unless there's an actual problem right in front of me.
Have these focus problems gotten noticeably worse recently compared with how you usually are?

Well, um... not exactly worse like out of nowhere, but it's been really bad for a while now. I'd say it became a huge issue when I took on all those extra charge-nurse responsibilities, which was... almost two years ago now? Yeah, two years in October. October is my favorite month, actually. I love Halloween. I usually go all out decorating my porch. Last year I made this giant spiderweb out of beef netting—you know, the stuff butchers use to tie up roasts? If you stretch it out and cut holes in it, it looks incredibly realistic. I spent like three hours stapling it to my gutters, and then it rained for a week straight and the whole thing sagged and looked terrible. The kids in the neighborhood still liked it, though. There's this one little boy next door who dressed up as a mailbox. A literal blue USPS mailbox. His dad made it out of cardboard, and it even had a little slot where you could drop the candy in. It was the cutest thing I've ever seen. I gave him full-size Snickers bars. You have to be the house with the full-size candy bars, right? Otherwise, what's the point? 

But yeah... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the focus stuff. So yeah, since I took on that charge-nurse role a couple years ago, it's just been a major, major problem.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

No, not really. I mean, I get frustrated with myself, like I said, but I'm not depressed. I still like doing things when I actually get around to them. Like my garden—I have this huge vegetable garden in my backyard. Well, it's supposed to be huge, but I got really behind on weeding it this year because of all the overtime at the hospital. Have you ever tried to grow tomatoes from seed? It is so much harder than buying the little starter plants at the nursery. You have to get the grow lights just right, and if they don't have enough air circulation, they get this weird fuzzy mold on the dirt. I bought this tiny little fan to put next to them, but my cat kept trying to eat the blades. He's a rescue, an orange tabby. They say orange cats all share one brain cell, and I honestly believe it. He'll just sit there staring at a blank wall for twenty minutes, and then suddenly sprint across the house like something is chasing him. I bought him this incredibly expensive automated laser toy so he'd stop waking me up at 3 AM, but he completely ignores it and just plays with the cardboard box it came in. Cats are so weird like that. 

But um, no, I don't feel depressed or down. Just overwhelmed with work and my brain not cooperating.
